    Glasshouse

    No listings. No asking prices. No agents.

    Every figure here is a recorded sale or a lodged rental bond from NSW Government records. Nothing you type leaves your browser.
    How the numbers workMethods, definitions and what to watch for
    Buy or rent
    Compares your net worth after the holding period (10 years by default) from buying the suburb's median home against renting a similar one and investing the difference. The buyer ends with the home's value after selling costs, less the loan left. The renter ends with the deposit, stamp duty and any monthly savings, invested and taxed at the lower earner's rate. Price growth blends the suburb's 10-year record with its region's, capped. Loan principal counts as saving, not cost. Every input is under Assumptions.
    Borrowing and deposit
    A rough guide, not a lender's assessment: after-tax income less living costs and other repayments must cover the loan at your rate plus a buffer. Lenders use their own living-cost floors, so yours may come out lower. Your cash pays stamp duty and costs first; the rest is deposit. Under 20% deposit, approximate mortgage insurance (1% to 5% of the loan) is added, unless you tick the 5% Deposit Scheme (first home buyers, up to $1.5m in Sydney). First home buyer duty uses the NSW exemption to $800k and an approximate concession to $1m.
    Prices and the time slider
    Each month shows the median of the 12 months of sales before it, so the map moves smoothly but turns a few months late. A chosen period compares the 12-month median at its start and end. Sales count once they settle, usually 6 to 7 weeks after contract, so figures trail the market by about that much. Suburbs marked "new" have under 10 years of sales and use their region's growth.
    What's left out of medians
    One price covering several homes (a developer buying a row of houses), and sales over 5 times or under a fifth of the suburb's typical price that year (development sites, family transfers). Both stay on the map: choose "Unusual prices" in the sales bar. Suburbs with fewer than 15 sales are left out of comparisons, because one sale can swing their median.
    Houses and units
    A sale is a unit when it's on a strata title, so most villas and many townhouses count as units. Rents come from bond lodgements by postcode, from 2021, where townhouses are grouped with houses. Lots later split into a duplex or units are marked as subdivided, with no value estimate.
    Before 2001
    The 1990 to 2000 records have no settlement date (estimated at contract plus 6 weeks) and no residence or strata flags, so they're classified from zoning and the land description.
